about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Nothing new on supply; Wednesday's slide was macro-driven (strong dollar, weaker grains and crude), not cotton-specific. Dec is in first-notice week below its supports, so delivery flows and high-grade certs matter more than the crop story near term — they are not a comfort for old-crop longs until Mar takes over.
events: Dec cotton fell with outside markets on Wednesday, trading near 75 (Barchart)
Texas yield cut again in USDA's November forecast, backing the short-crop case (RFD-TV)

sugar.fundamental: Brazil still drives it: the weaker real makes Brazilian raws cheaper to sell abroad and sugar keeps paying over hydrous ethanol, so mills stay sugar-heavy. USDA's lower global production estimate is a mild offset, but it has not stopped Mar slipping to the 18.0 support area.
events: Raws slid as the Brazilian real weakened (Barchart)
USDA's biannual outlook sees lower world sugar output (ADMIS)

coffee.fundamental: Price news is bearish on bigger expected Brazil and global supplies, but the deliverability picture still leans tight: ICE certified arabica keeps drawing (about 201k bags, down roughly 14% in a month) and Brazil's November shipments are running at a solid pace that has yet to restock ICE or Antwerp. Net: price weak, stocks story still supportive.
events: Arabica fell sharply on expectations of larger Brazil and global supplies (Barchart)
ICE certified arabica stocks still falling; Cecafé shows Nov exports at 2.29m bags through the 17th (ICE, Cecafé)
Fair Trade USA raises its minimum coffee prices (Daily Coffee News)

cocoa.fundamental: Supply worries keep easing: rising ICE certified stocks and better crop prospects outweigh the earlier rain-related slowdown in Ivory Coast port deliveries. Demand evidence is still thin, so the bias stays bearish while Mar tests the 4,978 support.
events: Improved supply prospects pushed cocoa lower; Mar down about 3% near 5,025 (Barchart)
Heavy rains had slowed bean transport to Ivorian ports last week (Reuters, Barchart)
Ghana plans to phase out raw bean exports by 2030 (Reuters)
